messages:
Alex H: heads-up, eu-west4 bootstrap failed during node rollout — ~40% of GPU nodes are NotReady after autoscaling, kubelet OOMs on some, and image pulls are timing out. :rotating_light:
Priya S: ok can you paste the node status + kubelet logs?
Alex H: ``kubectl get nodes -o wide`` shows nodes join then immediately go NotReady, kernel taints + docker runtime errors. journalctl shows `failed to load nvidia module` and `kubelet: container runtime not ready`.
Marco T: did we pick the right AMI for the new AZ? we recently pushed an AMI with the new nvidia driver packaging. If launch template points to old AMI that mismatches driver / kernel, that explains it.
Alex H: launch template points to `ami-2026-eu4-base-v1` (from image pipeline). I grepped user-data — it's missing the driver install step, looks like a pipeline regression.
Sasha L: also seeing a bunch of CNI flaps in logs: pods can't access API server IPs intermittently. MTU mismatch between VPC ENI (9001) and CNI (1500) causing fragmentation for large pulls?
Priya S: ugh. two separate failures then: AMI/user-data missing driver, and CNI/MTU mismatch. Which to prioritize?
Alex H: image pulls failing because kernel driver absent -> runtime crashes -> kubelet restarts. But the MTU issue makes e2e networking flaky. both need fixes before handoff.
Sasha L: quick mitigation: start a new rolling group with launch template override that injects `#!/bin/bash
set -e
apt-get update && apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-XXX` in user-data to validate nodes spin up. I can push a temp launch-template override.
Marco T: +1, do it in a canary group first (2 nodes). Also add `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` in user-data to help with MTU while we debug CNI config.
Alex H: doing canary now. infra-bot: deploy status?
infra-bot: Canary ASG created (asg-eu4-canary-176850), 2 instances launching. Instance IDs: i-0abc..., i-0def...
Sasha L: canary node i-0abc came up Ready after user-data ran, nvidia modules present. kubelet stabilized. image pulls succeeded for test pods. :thumbsup: 
Priya S: good. What about the MTU?
Sasha L: the canary still shows occasional packet drops for 2x ~1500B packets during container image pulls. Checked `ip link` on ENI: MTU is 9001 but CNI plugin expects 1500. Our previous regions had CNI set to jumbo frames; the new VPC provider sets different defaults. Need to align the VPC or set CNI config to 9001.
Marco T: we should not change cluster CNI default silently. Plan: 1) patch launch template for production groups to include driver install, 2) add preflight check in provisioner that validates AMI + user-data executes driver install, 3) add automated MTU preflight that checks VPC ENI MTU matches expected CNI MTU and fail the cluster create if mismatch.
Alex H: agree. Also we need to handle images failing to pull due to NAT gateway route missing in new subnets — saw 502s in image registry logs.
Priya S: who authorized the new subnet creation? looks like the terraform network module didn't attach the NAT route to the private route tables in eu-west4-b.
Marco T: that was me, I merged the network change with the wrong variable set for `enable_nat=true` in one region. My bad.
Marco T: immediate action: I'll reapply the network TF to add NAT routes. Sasha can we keep canary nodes until NAT is in place to validate?
Sasha L: yes. Keeping canary.
Alex H: operational decisions: pause wider cluster rollouts in eu-west4 until NAT + AMI fixes + MTU preflight are in place. We should also roll back any ASG that scaled beyond canary.
oncall: noted. marking as P1 for provisioning runbook follow-up. We'll coordinate a short SWAT.
Priya S: follow-ups for runbook: add AMI/user-data unit tests, add a `preflight.sh` that runs on the provisioner CI: checks AMI contains `/usr/lib/nvidia` and that CNI mtu from kube-proxy/cni config equals expected, validate route tables for NAT/egress.
Marco T: will open a PR with the TF fix for NAT and a separate PR to add the launch-template user-data.
Sasha L: I'll prepare a tiny validation job that runs `kubectl run --image=busybox mtu-check --restart=Never -- /bin/sh -c "ip link; wget -O- https://registry.redwood-internal/images/ping"` and fails if MTU or pulls fail. We can wire this into the region gating.
Alex H: good. Also create a rollback playbook entry: how to pin to the previous stable AMI and scale down problematic ASGs.
Priya S: adding action items: 1) Marco - TF NAT fix (ETA 30m) 2) Marco - launch-template PR for user-data (ETA 45m) 3) Sasha - validation job + sysctl mitigation (ETA 1h) 4) Alex - update runbook + schedule handoff to platform-owner (ETA 2h)
infra-bot: Incident ticket created: INF-2026-1123, severity: HIGH, assignees: Alex H, Marco T, Sasha L
oncall: I'll join the SWAT in 5, looping in platform-owner and release-eng. Do we want a postmortem once stable?
Alex H: yes, blameless postmortem. Also require a checklist in the runbook before any future region bootstraps: AMI test, user-data lint, CNI/MTU check, route table NAT validation, in-region image registry health check.
Priya S: +1. We should also add an alert that fires when >10% of nodes in a new cluster report kernel driver missing errors within the first 30 minutes.
Sasha L: temporary mitigation applied, canary healthy for now. Will keep logs and follow up with exact commands and diff in the PR.
Alex H: thanks team — keeping this thread for the handoff notes. Will post runbook PR links + incident ticket when done.
